html:
The Matagalpa and Cacaopera were peoples of the central highlands of Nicaragua and of eastern El Salvador. They spoke related languages of the Misumalpan family, which also includes the languages of the Miskito and Mayangna.

They farmed maize, beans and cacao in mountain valleys. To the west lay the Nahua and Chorotega peoples of the Pacific side, and to the north the Lenca. Under Spanish rule their lands became haciendas and, later, coffee country. Their languages died out by the 20th century, but many communities around Matagalpa and Cacaopera still claim Indigenous identity.
